subject: Taxes
title: The French Revolution and Taxes
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The French Revolution and Taxes.

hook.text: In 1789, French commoners paid crushing taxes while nobles and clergy paid almost nothing.

buildup.text: The gabelle (salt tax), the taille (land tax), and the corvée (labor tax) fell entirely on the Third Estate.

discovery.text: When Louis XVI tried to tax nobles, they refused. He convened the Estates-General.

twist.text: The revolution abolished all feudal taxes on August 4, 1789. In one night, a thousand years of tax privilege ended.

climax.text: The French Revolution proved that tax inequality is a time bomb. Privilege without contribution destroys legitimacy.

punchline.text: Nobles paid nothing. Commoners paid everything. Revolution was inevitable.

quiz.question: Who was exempt from most taxes in pre-revolutionary France?
